{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=eacikgoz17_exp8_tur
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks-per-node=2
#   --partition=ai
#   --qos=ai
#   --account=ai
#   --gres=gpu:tesla_t4:1
#   --mem=20G
#   --time=7-0:0:0
#   --output=test-%j.out
#   --mail-type=ALL
#   --mail-user=eacikgoz17@ku.edu.tr

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 2 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=168h \
  --queue=ai \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm %j output naming using Flux job id.
exec >"test-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

# NOTE: Slurm --qos=ai has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: QoS-related priority/limits/preemption behavior may not be applied, changing queue time
# or job survivability.

# NOTE: Slurm --account=ai has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm --gres=gpu:tesla_t4:1 requests a specific GPU model (tesla_t4).
# Flux has no universal, portable directive for GPU type; only the count (--gpus=1) is requested.
# Performance implication: you may be scheduled on a different GPU model, affecting performance/compatibility.

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=20G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-user/--mail-type) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

echo "Setting stack size to unlimited..."
ulimit -s unlimited
ulimit -l unlimited
ulimit -a
echo

module load anaconda/3.6
source activate eacikgoz17
nvidia-smi
python main_tur.py

source deactivate
'
"
